links.outcome: Recommendation correctness, comparing RAG-grounded UroBot versus ungrounded ChatGPT rated by urologists
links.effect: UroBot outperformed ChatGPT on recommendation correctness (73% vs 50%; p<0.001), source attribution (74% vs 30%) and source verifiability (84% vs 35%).
links.quote: UroBot performed significantly better than ChatGPT in recommendation correctness (73 % vs. 50 %; p < 0.001), source attribution (74 % vs. 30 %; p < 0.001) and verifiability of sources (84 % vs. 35 %; p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Source verifiability and clinician trust with in-line references and source text previews versus none
links.effect: In-line references and source previews raised verifiability ratings (84% vs 35%) and clinicians preferred UroBot for accuracy, source verifiability and trust.
links.quote: Furthermore, clinicians consistently preferred UroBot for accuracy, source verifiability and trust.

links.outcome: Citation validity of ChatGPT outputs (non-existent, outdated, or non-specific citations)
links.effect: 28% of ChatGPT citations were non-existent or outdated and 83% lacked specific sections; UroBot achieved complete alignment on guideline sub-section and page level.
links.quote: Qualitative analysis showed that ChatGPT often produced vague or incorrect citations, with 28 % being non-existent or outdated and 83 % lacking specific sections, whereas UroBot achieved complete alignment on guideline sub-section and page level.

screen.reason: Evaluated whether adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with in-line source attribution and previews improves recommendation correctness, source verifiability, and clinician trust in a randomized reader study with 30 urologists.

primary.practice: retrieval-augmented generation with transparent source attribution
